یک سال پیش، یکی از سناتورهای باسابقه آمریکا چندان درباره مراکز داده (دیتا سنتر) فکر نمی‌کرد.

اما حالا، به گفته یکی از مشاورانش، دائما با اعضای دفترش درباره تاثیر این مراکز جلسه برگزار می‌کند و روی تدوین طرحی قانونی کار می‌کند که هدفش مهار گسترش سریع چنین مراکزی در سراسر آمریکا است.

یکی از مشاوران ارشد سیاست‌گذاری این سناتور دموکرات به بی‌بی‌سی گفت: «گاهی همین‌طور است؛ موضوعی ابتدا آرام و آهسته شروع می‌شود و بعد ناگهان شتاب می‌گیرد.» او به شرط ناشناس ماندن صحبت کرد، چون اجازه ندارد با رسانه‌ها در این زمینه حرف بزند.

چرخش ۱۸۰ درجه‌ای توجه این سناتور تقریبا به‌طور کامل نتیجه موج فزاینده مخالفت‌های عمومی بود؛ موجی که سیاستمداران را در سراسر آمریکا وادار کرده برای عقب نماندن از آن دست‌به‌کار شوند.

افکار عمومی به‌تدریج علیه گسترش مراکز داده موضع گرفته است؛ ساختمان‌های عظیم و انبارمانندی که توان پردازشی مورد نیاز برای فعالیت‌های اینترنتی را در خود جای می‌دهند.

مراکز داده با ردیف‌های متعدد تراشه‌های رایانه‌ای، که گاهی ارتفاع تجهیزات آن‌ها به بیش از دو متر می‌رسد، دیگر فقط زیرساخت اینترنت نیستند. آن‌ها اکنون به نمود فیزیکی رشد سریع و انفجاری فناوری هوش مصنوعی و نگرانی‌های مختلفی تبدیل شده‌اند که مردم با آن مرتبط می‌دانند.

آنجلیتا سوریانو، ساکن ایندیانا، به بی‌بی‌سی گفت: «نمی‌خواهم موش آزمایشگاهی این ماجرا باشم.»

درست روبه‌روی خانه او، آمازون در حال ساخت یک مرکز داده جدید است. پس از تکمیل، این مجموعه متشکل از ۲۶ ساختمان بیش از ۲ کیلومتر مربع از محله محل زندگی او را در بر خواهد گرفت و ۷۸۲ ژنراتور دیزلی در آن به‌ کار گرفته خواهد شد.

برخی مراکز داده حتی بزرگ‌ترند.

در اوهایو، قرار است در پروژه‌ای مشترک میان اوپن‌ای‌آی، انویدیا، اس‌بی انرژی و وزارت انرژی آمریکا مجموعه‌ای از مراکز داده ساخته شود که حدود شش مایل مربع، نزدیک به ۱۵/۵ کیلومتر مربع، وسعت خواهد داشت؛ تقریبا به اندازه بسیاری از شهرک‌های آمریکا.

گزیده‌ای از مهم‌ترین خبرها، گزارش‌های میدانی و گفت‌وگوهای اختصاصی را هر هفته در ایمیل خود دریافت کنید.

در حال حاضر حدود ۳ هزار مرکز داده در آمریکا فعال است و بر اساس گزارش مرکز پژوهشی پیو، این تعداد ممکن است طی چند سال آینده دو برابر شود.

ساخت مراکز داده عمدتا بر اساس مقررات و مجوزهای محلی انجام می‌شود. بنابراین قانون‌گذاران فدرال مانند سناتورهای آمریکا نقش محدودی در این روند دارند.

اما مخالفت با آن‌ها در آمریکا آن‌قدر سریع و شدید افزایش یافته که حالا سیاستمداران در همه سطوح تقریبا ناچارند موضعی مشخص اتخاذ کنند.

کلویی آتیو، مشاور سیاست‌گذاری هوش مصنوعی، گفت: «این فقط مسئله‌ای مربوط به جناح چپ نیست. در میان محافظه‌کاران هم مخالفت بسیار زیادی با مراکز داده وجود دارد. در هر دو حزب، هر کسی که موضع روشنی بیان کند و به آن پایبند بماند، می‌تواند از نظر سیاسی از آن بهره ببرد.»

مشاور سناتور آمریکایی که روی قانون‌گذاری مراکز داده کار می‌کند هم ارزیابی مشابهی داشت.

او گفت: «اینجا نیاز مشخصی به سیاست‌گذاری وجود دارد و ما می‌خواهیم این خلا را پر کنیم. مخالفت بزرگی در سراسر کشور شکل گرفته است، مردم آثار مراکز داده را می‌بینند و از آن خوششان نمی‌آید.»

همین موضوع بسیاری از سیاستمداران کنگره، حتی جمهوری‌خواهان، را مستقیما در برابر دونالد ترامپ، رئیس‌جمهور آمریکا، قرار داده است؛ کسی که از رشد بدون محدودیت فناوری هوش مصنوعی حمایت کرده است.

دونالد ترامپ مخالفت با مراکز داده را «توطئه‌ای بیمارگونه» توصیف کرده و گفته است مردم و شهرهایی که می‌کوشند مانع ساخت آن‌ها شوند «عقب‌مانده و فقیر» هستند.

این موضع ترامپ برای سیاستمداران دموکراتی که می‌خواهند در انتخابات میان‌دوره‌ای آرای شهروندان ناراضی یا مردد را جلب کنند، به فرصتی سیاسی تبدیل شده است.

بی‌بی‌سی با ساکنانی از ایندیانا، آریزونا، میشیگان، پنسیلوانیا و اورگن صحبت کرده است که همگی در سطح محلی علیه توسعه مراکز داده فعالیت می‌کنند.

بر اساس پژوهش مؤسسه «دیتا سنتر واچ»، در چند ماه نخست سال جاری شمار گروه‌های محلی که علیه گسترش مراکز داده سازماندهی می‌کنند، بیش از دو برابر شد و به ۸۳۳ گروه رسید؛ گروه‌هایی که تقریبا در همه ایالت‌های آمریکا فعال‌اند.

«دیتا سنتر واچ» داده‌هایی را برای بازیگران صنعت هوش مصنوعی جمع‌آوری می‌کند و بخشی از شرکت نوپای هوش مصنوعی «۱۰ای لبز» (10a Labs) به شمار می‌رود.

استفانی مالدونادو، مدیر سیاسی سازمان «لوچا»، یک گروه سازمان‌دهی اجتماعی مستقر در ایالت آریزونا، مخالفت‌ها با گسترش مراکز داده را به داستان «داوود و جالوت» تشبیه می‌کند؛ جنبشی که به گفته او چند سال پیش آغاز شد.

مالدونادو افزود: «مردم از مدت‌ها پیش آماده بودند جلو آن را بگیرند. حالا عصبانی‌اند.»

نظرسنجی ملی تازه‌ای نشان می‌دهد پس از جنگ با ایران و مسائل مختلف اقتصادی، مقررات هوش مصنوعی و مراکز داده از جمله موضوعات مهم برای رای‌دهندگان در این دوره انتخاباتی هستند.

طرفداران ساخت مراکز داده اغلب می‌گویند این پروژه‌ها شغل‌های بیشتر و با درآمد بالاتر برای جوامع محلی ایجاد می‌کنند.

اما پژوهش تازه موسسه بروکینگز، یک مرکز پژوهشی غیرحزبی، نشان داده است یک مرکز داده جدید بین ۱۰۰ تا ۲۰۰ شغل محلی ایجاد می‌کند؛ رقمی که به گفته این موسسه «کمتر از چیزی است که حامیان صنعت ادعا می‌کنند».

این پروژه‌ها همچنین عملا تاثیری بر سطح دستمزدهای محلی ندارند.

او به بی‌بی‌سی گفت که با وجود آنکه این تاسیسات به گونه‌ای طراحی شده‌اند که آب مورد نیاز خود را از طریق جمع‌آوری آب باران تامین کنند و انرژی مورد نیازشان را نیز خود تولید کنند، که رویکردی روزبه‌روز رایج‌تر در پروژه‌های بزرگ مراکز داده است، بسیاری از ساکنان منطقه از همان ابتدا با این طرح مخالفت کرده‌اند.

او گفت: «از همان لحظه اول سطح تنش آن‌قدر بالاست که تقریبا حتی نمی‌توان با ارائه واقعیت‌ها از این دیوار عبور کرد.»

تاماباتولا گفت در یک نشست اجتماعی اخیر تلاش کرده است با زنی که به‌شدت با پروژه مخالف بود، رو‌در‌رو صحبت کند.

او گفت: این زن صاف در چشمانم نگاه کرد و گفت: «از ایالت من برو بیرون.»

news.originalContent:
Photo by Garry Austin/Getty Images

Parents accused a youth sports travel company of misleading families into paying hotel booking fees and higher lodging costs by telling them their children could not compete unless they booked through its platform, according to a federal lawsuit.

The proposed class action against Team Travel Source challenges “stay-to-play” practices that tie tournament participation to designated hotel booking arrangements, adding to the costs families face beyond registration, equipment and travel. Attorney Karen Dahlberg O’Connell told the Daily Caller News Foundation that hundreds of parents contacted her legal team after the case was filed, reporting similar experiences across the country.

The lawsuit, filed in the Western District of Kentucky against The Complete Plan Inc., which operates as Team Travel Source, includes nine parents from seven states whose children participate in cheerleading and volleyball. The amended complaint alleges deceptive booking requirements, inadequately disclosed mandatory fees and misleading promises of discounted hotel rates.

Team Travel Source denied wrongdoing in a statement provided to the DCNF by Kelley Roberts.

“We deny participation in any alleged violation of the law in connection with the allegations in the proposed class action lawsuit or otherwise,” the company said, adding that it would address the allegations through counsel in the appropriate forum. “We have always run our company in an ethical way and truly appreciate everyone in the space.”

In court filings seeking dismissal, the company argued that tournament organizers established stay-to-play requirements and determine exemptions. It also said its checkout process disclosed fees before customers finalized reservations and that families received services including room blocks, booking assistance and customer support.

Kentucky mother Kate Russell alleged she booked three nights at an Atlanta hotel for $516.85, including $15 in booking service fees, after being told her daughter’s volleyball team could be disqualified if she did not reserve through the platform. A teammate’s family booked elsewhere and the child still competed, according to the complaint.

The parents also challenged mandatory charges labeled as booking, housing, cancellation convenience and premier property fees. Some applied per night even when a parent made a single reservation, the complaint alleges.

The company’s guarantee applies only to some events, excludes booking fees from rate comparisons and requires matching room types, amenities and cancellation terms. Membership and government rates are among its exclusions.

O’Connell described one parent who reported finding a cheaper room directly through a hotel but was denied an adjustment because the Team Travel Source reservation guaranteed access to a rollaway bed. The parent neither wanted nor needed that bed, O’Connell said.

The amended complaint also cites company marketing claiming more than $17 million in rebates paid to tournament organizers in 2025. Plaintiffs allege those payments were funded by inflated lodging costs and fees; that funding allegation remains disputed.

The company’s reach extended to more than 1,600 annual events in over 400 cities across 44 states, according to website figures cited in the complaint.

An Aspen Institute survey found families spent an average of $1,016 on one child’s primary sport in 2024, up 46% from 2019.

“I just want parents to have the freedom of choice in terms of how they stay and where they stay,” O’Connell told the DCNF.

The parents seek class certification, damages and court orders addressing the challenged practices. Team Travel Source asked the court to dismiss the amended complaint and filed its reply supporting that request on Wednesday.

news.originalContent:
با رای اعتماد نمایندگان مجلس مهرداد اخلاقی کتابچی وزیر دفاع ایران شد. او از مدیران با سابقه صنایع دفاعی و هوافضای در جمهوری اسلامی است اما تاکنون چهره‌ای کمتر شناخته‌شده برای عموم بوده است.

او  در نشست وبیناری علنی مجلس با ۲۳۷ رأی موافق، جایگزین عزیز نصیرزاده شد که با ۲۸۱ رای رکورد بالاترین رای اعتماد تاریخ جمهوری اسلامی را داشت اما در اولین روز جنگ ۴۰ روزه همراه چند فرمانده ارشد کشته شد.

در جلسه رای اعتماد، مسعود پزشکیان، رئیس جمهور، از آقای اخلاقی به عنوان فردی یاد کرد که سابقه همکاری با حسن تهرانی مقدم، محسن فخری‌زاده و امیرعلی حاجی‌زاده را داشته است و افزود که او در «لیست ترور» قرار داد.

حسن تهرانی مقدم و محسن فخری زاده که از اولی به عنوان «پدر برنامه موشکی» و دومی به عنوان «پدر برنامه هسته‌ای» ایران نام برده می‌شود، در سال‌های ۱۳۹۰ و ۱۳۹۹ ترور شدند. امیرعلی حاجی‌زاده، فرمانده هوافضای سپاه هم  در جنگ ۱۲ روزه در حمله اسرائیل کشته شد.

رئیس‌جمهور ایران با اشاره به «۴۲ سال» سابقه آقای اخلاقی گفت همین که او مدت‌هاست در فهرست «ترور» است و آمریکا هم او را تحریم کرده است، نشانه صلاحیت اوست.

مهرداد اخلاقی کتابچی در دفاع از خود گفت: «پس از جنگ ۱۲ روزه، قابلیت‌های دفاعی به‌گونه‌ای روزآمد شده‌اند که برآوردها و محاسبات دشمن را تغییر داده و تردیدی عمیق در میان دشمنان درباره استمرار جنگ ایجاد کرده‌اند.»

مهرداد اخلاقی اگرچه برای رسانه‌ها چهره‌ای ناشناس بود اما آمریکا ۱۹ سال پیش او را در فهرست تحریم‌هایش قرار داده بود. آقای پزشکیان امروز گفت‌ تحریم‌ شدن او خود دلیل صلاحیتش است.

نام آقای اخلاقی در قطعنامه ۱۷۴۷ شورای امنیت سازمان ملل متحد  ایران هم ذکر شده است. در آن قطعنامه از کشورهای دنیا خواسته شده‌ ارتباط با شرکت‌های ایرانی فعال در انرژی هسته‌ای را محدود کنند

ساعتی پس از رای اعتماد مجلس، احمد وحیدی، فرمانده کل سپاه پاسداران و امیر حاتمی، فرمانده ارتش انتخاب او را تبریک گفتند و از او حمایت کردند.

گزیده‌ای از مهم‌ترین خبرها، گزارش‌های میدانی و گفت‌وگوهای اختصاصی را هر هفته در ایمیل خود دریافت کنید.

وقتی نام مهرداد اخلاقی به عنوان وزیر دفاع جدید ایران مطرح شد، عکسی در رسانه‌ها نداشت.

۲۱ مهر زمانی که در کمیسیون ویژه مجلس برای رسیدگی به صلاحیتش حاضر شد، شماری از رسانه‌های ایران با تیتر ‌«اولین تصویر از مهرداد اخلاقی کتابچی» این جلسه را پوشش دادند.

او بر خلاف مجید ابن‌الرضا، سرپرست وقت وزارت دفاع، که با عنوان و یونیفرم نظامی در مراسم حاضر می‌شود، با کت‌وشلوار به جلسه کمیسیون ویژه رفته بود.

آقای اخلاقی کتابچی متولد ۱۳۳۷ است و بنا به گزارش کمیسیون امنیت ملی و سیاست خارجی مجلس شورای اسلامی، مدرک کارشناسی مهندسی شیمی از دانشگاه صنعتی امیرکبیر و کارشناسی ارشد مدیریت راهبردی از دانشگاه صنعتی مالک اشتر دارد.

او مدتی ریاست گروه صنعتی شهید باقری را بر عهده داشته که در طراحی و توسعه و تولید سامانه‌های موشکی از جمله موشک‌های بالستیک فعالیت می‌کرده است.

آقای اخلاقی در آبان ۱۳۹۳، در دولت حسن روحانی، با حکم حسین دهقان، وزیر وقت دفاع، به عنوان مدیرعامل سازمان صنایع هوافضای وزارت دفاع (ساصد) منصوب شد.

دفاع‌پرس که اخبار نظامی ایران را پوشش می‌دهد از آقای اخلاقی به عنوان چهره‌ای یاد کرده است که در توسعه ظرفیت‌های موشکی ایران نقش داشته و در در ‌«حوزه پیشران‌های سوخت جامد» جایگاه ویژه‌ای داشته است.

پیشران‌های سوخت جامد، در توسعه برنامه موشک‌های بالستیک ایران و به طور خاص افزایش برد، آمادگی عملیاتی و کاهش زمان آماده‌سازی و پرتاب نقشی اساسی داشته است.

مهرداد اخلاقی در بخشی از معرفی خود گفته بود از سال ۱۳۶۳ تا ۱۳۷۳ صرفا در حوزه تحقیقات فعالیت داشته و از سال ۱۳۷۳ وارد بخش تولید شده است.

آقای اخلاقی ارائه جزئیات برنامه‌هایش به مجلس را به مصلحت امنیتی نداست اما تاکید کرد که طبقه‌بندی سری، سازه‌های امن برای تولید محصولات و حمایت از جبهه مقاومت تاکید کرد.

آقای اخلاقی وعده داده که توسعه توان موشکی به ویژه موشک‌های زمین به زمین و کروز و همچنین پدافند را در اولویت برنامه‌هایش قرار دهد.

او همچنین گفت که اولین جنگنده سنگین که کاملا ساخت ایران است سال آینده به پرواز در‌آید.

مهرداد اخلاقی در بخشی از توضیحات خودش به مجلس گفت: «از ۹ اسفند [آغاز حمله آمریکا و اسرائیل به ایران] تا امروز، محل کار من در سازمان صنایع دفاع در مجاورت ساختمان‌هایی بود که مورد اصابت موشک قرار گرفته بودند. با وجود اصابت ۲۵ موشک به ساختمان محل کارم، حتی از فاصله ۱۰۰متری آن نیز خارج نشدم و محل استقرارم را تغییر ندادم.»

مجتبی خامنه‌ای اخیر در پیامی از فرماندهان نظامی ایران علی الخصوص فرمانده هوافضا سپاه خواسته بود تا امنیت خود را در اولویت قرار دهند.

او در پیام مرداد ماه خود خطاب به مجید موسوی، فرمانده نیروی هوافضای سپاه، نوشته بود: که «مراقبت از جان عزیز خودتان و همه برادران خواسته مؤکد اینجانب است.»

یکی از نخستین اظهارات مهرداد اخلاقی در حاشیه جلسه رای اعتماد مجلس در پاسخ خبرنگاران درباره احتمال استفاده آمریکا از «مادر بمب‌ها» بود که گفت:

«ما تدابیر لازم را برای این موضوع اندیشیده‌ایم و خیالمان راحت است. با اطمینان کار خود را انجام می‌دهیم.»

او گفت که رئیس‌جمهور آمریکا «باید به فکر این باشد که نیروهایش را سالم از منطقه ما خارج کند. اگر یک بمب بیندازد، باید ببیند چند نفر از نیروهایش را باید به‌صورت افقی از منطقه خارج کند.»

به گفته وزیر دفاع جدید ایران، «همین موضوع باعث شده است که آمریکا تاکنون از این اقدام خودداری کند. البته اگر تهدیدهایش را از شعار به عمل تبدیل کند، نتیجه‌اش را خواهد دید.»

ساعتی پس از رای اعتماد مجلس، احمد وحیدی، فرمانده کل سپاه پاسداران و امیر حاتمی، فرمانده ارتش انتخاب او را تبریک گفتند و از او حمایت کردند.

گزیده‌ای از مهم‌ترین خبرها، گزارش‌های میدانی و گفت‌وگوهای اختصاصی را هر هفته در ایمیل خود دریافت کنید.

وقتی نام مهرداد اخلاقی به عنوان وزیر دفاع جدید ایران مطرح شد، عکسی در رسانه‌ها نداشت.

۲۱ مهر زمانی که در کمیسیون ویژه مجلس برای رسیدگی به صلاحیتش حاضر شد، شماری از رسانه‌های ایران با تیتر ‌«اولین تصویر از مهرداد اخلاقی کتابچی» این جلسه را پوشش دادند.

او بر خلاف مجید ابن‌الرضا، سرپرست وقت وزارت دفاع، که با عنوان و یونیفرم نظامی در مراسم حاضر می‌شود، با کت‌وشلوار به جلسه کمیسیون ویژه رفته بود.

آقای اخلاقی کتابچی متولد ۱۳۳۷ است و بنا به گزارش کمیسیون امنیت ملی و سیاست خارجی مجلس شورای اسلامی، مدرک کارشناسی مهندسی شیمی از دانشگاه صنعتی امیرکبیر و کارشناسی ارشد مدیریت راهبردی از دانشگاه صنعتی مالک اشتر دارد.

او مدتی ریاست گروه صنعتی شهید باقری را بر عهده داشته که در طراحی و توسعه و تولید سامانه‌های موشکی از جمله موشک‌های بالستیک فعالیت می‌کرده است.

آقای اخلاقی در آبان ۱۳۹۳، در دولت حسن روحانی، با حکم حسین دهقان، وزیر وقت دفاع، به عنوان مدیرعامل سازمان صنایع هوافضای وزارت دفاع (ساصد) منصوب شد.

دفاع‌پرس که اخبار نظامی ایران را پوشش می‌دهد از آقای اخلاقی به عنوان چهره‌ای یاد کرده است که در توسعه ظرفیت‌های موشکی ایران نقش داشته و در در ‌«حوزه پیشران‌های سوخت جامد» جایگاه ویژه‌ای داشته است.

پیشران‌های سوخت جامد، در توسعه برنامه موشک‌های بالستیک ایران و به طور خاص افزایش برد، آمادگی عملیاتی و کاهش زمان آماده‌سازی و پرتاب نقشی اساسی داشته است.

مهرداد اخلاقی در بخشی از معرفی خود گفته بود از سال ۱۳۶۳ تا ۱۳۷۳ صرفا در حوزه تحقیقات فعالیت داشته و از سال ۱۳۷۳ وارد بخش تولید شده است.

آقای اخلاقی ارائه جزئیات برنامه‌هایش به مجلس را به مصلحت امنیتی نداست اما تاکید کرد که طبقه‌بندی سری، سازه‌های امن برای تولید محصولات و حمایت از جبهه مقاومت تاکید کرد.

آقای اخلاقی وعده داده که توسعه توان موشکی به ویژه موشک‌های زمین به زمین و کروز و همچنین پدافند را در اولویت برنامه‌هایش قرار دهد.

او همچنین گفت که اولین جنگنده سنگین که کاملا ساخت ایران است سال آینده به پرواز در‌آید.

مهرداد اخلاقی در بخشی از توضیحات خودش به مجلس گفت: «از ۹ اسفند [آغاز حمله آمریکا و اسرائیل به ایران] تا امروز، محل کار من در سازمان صنایع دفاع در مجاورت ساختمان‌هایی بود که مورد اصابت موشک قرار گرفته بودند. با وجود اصابت ۲۵ موشک به ساختمان محل کارم، حتی از فاصله ۱۰۰متری آن نیز خارج نشدم و محل استقرارم را تغییر ندادم.»

مجتبی خامنه‌ای اخیر در پیامی از فرماندهان نظامی ایران علی الخصوص فرمانده هوافضا سپاه خواسته بود تا امنیت خود را در اولویت قرار دهند.

او در پیام مرداد ماه خود خطاب به مجید موسوی، فرمانده نیروی هوافضای سپاه، نوشته بود: که «مراقبت از جان عزیز خودتان و همه برادران خواسته مؤکد اینجانب است.»

یکی از نخستین اظهارات مهرداد اخلاقی در حاشیه جلسه رای اعتماد مجلس در پاسخ خبرنگاران درباره احتمال استفاده آمریکا از «مادر بمب‌ها» بود که گفت:

«ما تدابیر لازم را برای این موضوع اندیشیده‌ایم و خیالمان راحت است. با اطمینان کار خود را انجام می‌دهیم.»

او گفت که رئیس‌جمهور آمریکا «باید به فکر این باشد که نیروهایش را سالم از منطقه ما خارج کند. اگر یک بمب بیندازد، باید ببیند چند نفر از نیروهایش را باید به‌صورت افقی از منطقه خارج کند.»

به گفته وزیر دفاع جدید ایران، «همین موضوع باعث شده است که آمریکا تاکنون از این اقدام خودداری کند. البته اگر تهدیدهایش را از شعار به عمل تبدیل کند، نتیجه‌اش را خواهد دید.»

GREEN BAY, Wis. — Jordan Love threw a touchdown pass and also scored on a 1-yard keeper and the Green Bay Packers held Dallas’ high-powered offense in check and beat the Cowboys 23-13 in a penalty-filled game Sunday night.

Love went 23 of 41 for 276 yards to help the Packers improve to 11-1-1 in their last 13 meetings with the Cowboys, including a 40-all tie last season at Arlington, Texas. A 9-yard touchdown pass to Matthew Golden capped Green Bay’s first series and put the Packers ahead for good.

The Packers (4-2) have won three straight as they await the return of three-time Pro Bowl running back Josh Jacobs, who comes off the commissioner’s exempt list Monday. Jacobs hasn’t played all season and pleaded no contest last month to two misdemeanor charges stemming from an altercation with his then-girlfriend in May.

Green Bay intercepted Dak Prescott twice to thwart scoring opportunities. Prescott went 34 of 54 for 258 yards. He threw a 6-yard touchdown pass to Ryan Flournoy with 44 seconds left, but couldn’t connect with CeeDee Lamb on a 2-point conversion attempt.

The game featured 22 penalties — 11 by each team. Dallas had 108 penalty yards, while Green Bay had 96.

Love’s night could have been even better.

Golden dropped what would have been a 43-yard touchdown and couldn’t complete the catch on a potential 23-yard score in the second quarter. A potential 26-yard touchdown pass went in and out of Christian Watson’s hands in the third quarter, though that pass was deflected in the end zone by Dallas’ Malachi Lawrence.

The Lambeau Field fireworks started prematurely after Golden couldn’t hang on to the 23-yarder even as the officials were signaling the incompletion. Green Bay still scored a touchdown after one of those drops and settled for Trey Smack field goals after the other two.

Golden still caught six passes for 104 yards, plus the early touchdown. Love went 6 of 8 for 109 yards on that opening possession, a 90-yard drive during which the Packers withstood a couple of penalties.

Dallas (2-4) trailed 17-0 at halftime, the first time the Cowboys went scoreless in the first half of a game since Nov. 7, 2021, when they were down 16-0 in an eventual 30-16 loss to Denver.

Prescott’s two interceptions proved costly.

The Cowboys faced second-and-8 from Green Bay’s 17 when Prescott absorbed a punishing hit from Zaire Franklin while throwing an incompletion. On the next play, Evan Williams picked off a pass across the middle that was intended for Lamb.

Dallas had a first down from Green Bay’s 23 on its next drive before a holding penalty pushed it back to the 33. The Cowboys had first-and-15 from the 28 when Lamb fell on a route, enabling Packers rookie Brandon Cisse to make his first career interception.

Green Bay capitalized on that second turnover by driving 77 yards and scoring on Love’s 1-yard sneak with 23 seconds left in the half.

Dallas scored on a 1-yard run from Javonte Williams early in the third quarter. Green Bay extended the lead on a pair of field goals by Smack.

A positive development for Dallas was an improved performance from its defense, which entered the night allowing a league-high 6.4 yards per play.

Dallas’ defense held a players-only meeting in the days leading up to this game. The Cowboys also brought in veteran defensive assistant Mike Pettine to assist first-year defensive coordinator Christian Parker.

Dee Winters made a diving catch late in the first quarter for Dallas’ first interception of the season. Winters then got up and weaved between multiple defenders to run over 40 yards for an apparent touchdown, but a replay review determined he was touched by Golden while still on the ground.

Cowboys: WR KaVontae Turpin left with a rib injury in the first quarter. Winters hurt his ankle in the second quarter.

Packers: CB Brandon Cisse left with a stinger in the second half.

Cowboys: At Philadelphia on Oct. 26.

Packers: At Detroit next Sunday.

news.originalContent:
Pope Leo pledges a gradual return to duties in an address to the Catholic faithful in St Peter’s Square at the Vatican.

Pope Leo XIV has thanked some 15,000 Catholic faithful gathered in St Peter’s Square during his Sunday address, his first major public appearance since lung cancer surgery.

“Now that this delicate phase is behind me, I will gradually resume my activities, always with God’s help and your prayers,” Leo said.

The 71-year-old pontiff addressed the crowd from a window overlooking the square at the Vatican, where a week ago on the same occasion of the traditional Angelus blessing, he revealed that a nodule had been found in his lung and would be surgically removed.

The operation confirmed he had adenocarcinoma, the most common type of lung cancer.

Test results to determine whether the cancer has spread are still pending.

Leo said the experience of the past week “has made me feel especially close to those facing illness and infirmity”.

He told the crowd that he had “truly felt your support” and expressed “particular gratitude to the doctors, nurses and all the staff at Gemelli Hospital” in Rome, where he was treated.

The pope paused for a moment and waved before retreating into his apartment in the Apostolic Palace.

A delegation from Africa, in Rome for a Catholic meeting, danced and ululated after the pope’s blessing.

“He was always in our prayers when he was sick, and we are happy to see him today,″ Alain Kalembu of the Democratic Republic of the Congo said. “This is an expression of our joy.”

Meanwhile, Claire Holland from Jacksonville, Florida, United States, said she felt “very blessed” to be present for the pope’s return to his flock.

There had been doubts that a planned papal voyage to Uruguay, Argentina and Peru in November would go ahead.

The Vatican’s secretary of state, Cardinal Pietro Parolin, told journalists on Friday that the pope may need to adjust the pace of his schedule “according to the condition of his health”.

But Leo’s surgeon, Stefano Margaritora, told Vatican News he believed there were “no clinical reasons why the trip should not go ahead”.

Latin Americans in the crowd in St Peter’s Square welcomed the news.

“We are all hoping for his recovery, and that he has gotten through the situation well. We know that he is OK, and we’re pleased,” Soledad Espinosa from Ecuador said.

St. John’s is honoring the late Kenny Klein this season by keeping the seat next to Coach Rick Pitino at the scorer’s table empty and adding a black band onto their jerseys with the letters, “K.K.”

The Sports Information Hall of Famer died June 25 at age 66 after a tragic episode at a dinner a few weeks prior. Klein retired in 2022 after spending nearly 40 years at Louisville. He helped out his close friend Pitino at St. John’s the past two years in the communications department.

“His wife [Donna] is going to be with us both home and away, which is big for us. On a personal level, it’s been a really horrendous summer,” Pitino said after St. John’s 104-99 exhibition victory over Rutgers in quadruple overtime at the Garden. “Not since 9/11 have I felt so sad, losing a person right in front of you who I love so much. We’ll keep honoring him. I keep thinking of him. My heart breaks for his wife. I miss him terribly.”

Throughout last season, Pitino promised Klein he would continue to coach as long as Klein stayed on with him at St. John’s.

“I believe he would’ve stayed,” Pitino said. “It’s sad, but life can be very sad. It’s a moment I’ll never forget. It’s a moment I cry about all the time. … We got to fight through it. Kenny would want us to fight through it.”

St. John’s unveiled a Ring of Honor at the Garden on Sunday. The 10 members are also part of the Legacy Honors, created in 2006. The current names are: Lou Carnesecca, Chris Mullin, Walter Berry, Mark Jackson, Sonny Dove, Tony Jackson, Joe Lapchick, Dick McGuire, Malik Sealy and Alan Seiden.

At some point this season, there will be a ceremony adding Zuby Ejiofor to the Ring of Honor. There is also talk of retiring jersey numbers, something St. John’s hasn’t previously done, according to athletic director Ed Kull.

“I believe he would’ve stayed,” Pitino said. “It’s sad, but life can be very sad. It’s a moment I’ll never forget. It’s a moment I cry about all the time. … We got to fight through it. Kenny would want us to fight through it.”

St. John’s unveiled a Ring of Honor at the Garden on Sunday. The 10 members are also part of the Legacy Honors, created in 2006. The current names are: Lou Carnesecca, Chris Mullin, Walter Berry, Mark Jackson, Sonny Dove, Tony Jackson, Joe Lapchick, Dick McGuire, Malik Sealy and Alan Seiden.

At some point this season, there will be a ceremony adding Zuby Ejiofor to the Ring of Honor. There is also talk of retiring jersey numbers, something St. John’s hasn’t previously done, according to athletic director Ed Kull.

news.originalContent:
Brazil’s president and his opponent lob a barrage of attacks on each other in debate a week before the October 25 vote.

Brazil’s President Luiz Inacio Lula da Silva and right-wing Senator Flavio Bolsonaro fired off a barrage of personal attacks during their first debate a week before a tight presidential run-off.

In a chaotic exchange on Sunday, the two men called each other “liar” multiple times, accused each other of corruption, dragged up various scandals, and clashed on issues from public security to healthcare.

Lula said Bolsonaro was “a habitual liar” and a “thug”, and physically distanced himself on stage from the candidate he called a “militiaman”, alluding to his alleged ties to Rio de Janeiro’s paramilitary groups.

Bolsonaro, who led the first-round election with 47 percent to Lula’s 45 percent, said it was better to keep Lula at a distance “because my wallet could be stolen”.

Throughout the debate, Bolsonaro, 45, the son of former President Jair Bolsonaro, paced behind Lula, shaking his head, smirking and scoffing as his adversary spoke.

The 80-year-old Lula, who is seeking a fourth term, demanded an explanation regarding a corruption investigation involving the older Bolsonaro, a question his opponent dodged.

The younger Bolsonaro responded by calling Lula a “clown”, and then parried by bringing up a potential corruption case involving one of the president’s sons.

Jair Bolsonaro has been under house arrest while serving a 27-year sentence connected to efforts to overturn the 2022 election, which he lost to Lula.

Flavio Bolsonaro hammered away at the top concerns of Brazilians, such as the cost of living and crime, and accused Lula of “reckless spending” to get re-elected, referring to various social measures the president has announced during the campaign.

Lula countered by asking Bolsonaro about his plans to emulate the drastic public spending cuts implemented by Argentina’s right-wing president, Javier Milei.

Bolsonaro dodged the question throughout the debate and pivoted to different topics.

When his father’s handling of the COVID-19 pandemic came up, Bolsonaro admitted that this “wasn’t an area where we saw the best results during Bolsonaro’s presidency. I’ll offer a mea culpa here.”

Lula also sought to portray his opponent as out of touch with poor Brazilians, saying Bolsonaro had never used the country’s public healthcare system or taken a bus.

“My opponent only knows about buses from books. He has never even stepped foot on one. He has no idea what the world of work is like,” Lula said.

Ahead of Sunday’s debate, supporters of each candidate gathered en masse in public to show their allegiance.

Pro-Bolsonaro crowds wearing Brazil’s national colours of yellow, green and blue packed Paulista Avenue in Sao Paulo’s financial centre, where the candidate addressed the crowd.

Lula supporters wearing red, symbolic of his Workers’ Party, filled Brasilia’s plaza of government buildings, while students backing the president protested against Bolsonaro in Rio de Janeiro.

“We need the current government to remain in power. If another government comes in, we’re, excuse my language, screwed,” said Lula supporter Sonia Maria at the Brasilia rally.

“I don’t like bandits. Out with Lula!” said Bolsonaro backer Vera de Sousa in Sao Paulo.

Also on Sunday, Brazil’s federal police asked the country’s Supreme Court to open an investigation into Bolsonaro over a money laundering accusation involving a lawyer close to him.

The presidential candidate is already under investigation for his links to Daniel Vorcaro, a disgraced former banker who financed a movie about Jair Bolsonaro’s life.

Lula spent 580 days in prison in ⁠2018 and 2019 on a corruption conviction that was later annulled over flaws in the investigation and legal proceedings.

Polls suggest a close race for the October 25 run-off, with Flavio Bolsonaro holding a slight advantage after finishing nearly 2 percentage points ahead of Lula in the first round on October 4.

Both candidates hope to engage the 33 million voters who stayed home in the first ⁠round, equal to about one in five eligible voters.

Sunday’s debate was the first between Lula and Bolsonaro after the candidates both ⁠declined previous opportunities. A second debate is scheduled for October 23, just ahead of the run-off.

news.originalContent:
See more of our coverage in your search results.

There were a handful of questionable coaching decisions and plays that were made at the end of the Giants’ 34-27 loss to the Saints that raised eyebrows.

The first was, while trailing 34-24 and driving into New Orleans territory with the ball, why the Giants didn’t kick a field goal with about three minutes remaining, to quickly cut the deficit to one score.

Get texts from Paul Schwartz with all the latest Giants news and insights, exclusive to Sports+ subscribers.

They moved the ball to the New Orleans 27-yard line with 2:56 remaining with two timeouts still to use, but opted to continue to play for the touchdown.

Right tackle Marcus Mbow was then called for a false start, and then quarterback J.J. McCarthy took a sack for an 8-yard loss.

The Giants then ran two more plays before settling for a Dominic Zvada 41-yard field goal to cut the lead to 34-27 with 2:04 remaining.

Giants head coach John Harbaugh defended his actions, saying, “We went for the field goal as fast as we could, as soon as we could with a reasonable chance to make it.”

Harbaugh then said he wanted to get a touchdown there, to cut the deficit to three points.

“We had a chance there to hit a couple of shots and maybe score a touchdown,” he said. “So, at that point, we were trying to get it done by 2:13. That’s the time management there. We weren’t able to quite get it done by 2:13 with the clock and all that. But in the ideal world, you’ll get it done by 2:13, that’s what we’re shooting for.”

Harbaugh added, “We’re trying to get two scores and the two-minute warning is valuable if we can get it done. We want that two-minute warning to count for us. That’s what we’re trying to get done. That’s the goal.”

The next mistake came when Zvada’s ensuing kickoff was short enough for Bryce Lance to field it 5 yards deep and return it, thus not allowing the Giants to stop the clock at the two-minute warning.

Lance’s return ended with 1:58 on the clock, essentially taking away a free timeout from the Giants.

“You want to kick it out of the back of the end zone, that’s the goal, that’s what we were hoping to do,” Harbaugh said.

Had Zvada done that, it would have forced New Orleans to run a play before the two-minute warning.

When asked why not just kick the ball out of bounds, Harbaugh said, “We thought he could get it out of the back of the end zone.”

Zvada said, “That was a mistake I made, and I’m going to have to work on. That goal was to try to get it out of the end zone, so we stop the clock before the two-minute warning and save a timeout.”

news.originalContent:
See more of our coverage in your search results.

First, the officials surprised Andrew Thomas by pulling him off the field.

Then, the Giants coaches surprised him by keeping him on the bench.

Get texts from Paul Schwartz with all the latest Giants news and insights, exclusive to Sports+ subscribers.

Thomas, one of the best left tackles in the NFL, didn’t return to the field in the fourth quarter after clearing a concussion evaluation on the sideline ordered by the independent spotter Sunday in a 34-27 loss to the Saints.

“That was interesting,” said Thomas, who is playing through an injured groin despite limited practice time. “The series before, I got up a little slow. When I went out there the next drive, they said I had to do the concussion protocol testing.”

Thomas looked antsy to get back in, but the Giants, who were rallying from a 24-point fourth-quarter deficit, were stuck with rookie J.C. Davis in his first career game.

Thomas did not get an explanation for the change.

“That was the coach’s decision,” Thomas said. “I listen to what the coach says.”

Thomas was not the only injury-related blow dealt to the Giants on Sunday. CB Greg Newsome II suffered a concussion and did not return.

WR Darnell Mooney (neck) was sidelined, leaving the Giants with three healthy receivers.

RG Sisi Mauigoa needed a postgame X-ray on an unspecified body part.

“I’m feeling good,” Mauigoa said, indicating he will be on the field again soon.

RT Jermaine Eluemunor (calf) was a surprise scratch after he was limited in Friday’s practice. Marcus Mbow started in his place.

Jason Pinnock and Ar’Darius Washington rotated at the safety position next to Jevón Holland with Tyler Nubin (neck) sidelined.

Sign up for Inside the Giants by Paul Schwartz, a weekly Sports+ exclusive.

Please provide a valid email.

By clicking above you agree to the Terms of Use and Privacy Policy.

Enjoy this Post Sports+ exclusive newsletter!

Pinnock forced a fumble that turned momentum when the Giants were down 34-10 with about 9:40 left in the fourth quarter.

“It’s in us to come back,” Pinnock said. “We’re more than capable.”

The only game in which a Giants quarterback had more fourth-quarter passing yards than J.J. McCarthy’s 243 on Sunday was when Eli Manning threw for 254 in a 36-25 loss against the Seahawks on Oct. 9, 2011.

McCarthy entered the game with about 11:31 left in the game after Jameis Winston threw his second interception. McCarthy went 11-for-21 with 243 yards passing, 26 rushing yards, a touchdown pass and an interception.

news.originalContent:
See more of our coverage in your search results.

Thousands of sailors remain stranded near the Strait of Hormuz amid escalating attacks on commercial ships, the United Nations’ top maritime official warned Sunday after Iran accused the US military of using an international emergency radio channel to threaten civilian crews.

The warning also came amid reports that 24 ships had been attacked on the waterway over roughly two weeks, underscoring growing concerns about maritime safety in the region, according to Financial Times.

“The situation continues to be severe and critical when it comes to international shipping,” International Maritime Organization (IMO) Secretary-General Arsenio Dominguez told Fox News Digital.

“There is a double blockade and too many vessels have been attacked, particularly in recent days.

“Seafarers have continued to perish in these attacks and around 6,000 seafarers remain trapped since the beginning of the conflict,” he warned, adding that his message was not to transit the Strait of Hormuz or put seafarers at risk “until we have guarantees.”

Dominguez’s warning followed an Oct. 9 letter to the IMO in which Iran alleged that the US military used VHF Channel 16, an internationally designated maritime distress and safety channel, to intimidate Iranian crews in the Persian Gulf.

“VHF Channel 16 has been repeatedly occupied for prolonged periods by the United States military forces operating in the Persian Gulf,” the letter stated.

“During such transmissions, Iranian seafarers have been addressed in Persian with threatening, abusive and provocative language and in certain instances urged to abandon their vessels.”

In a statement to Fox News Digital, US Central Command defended its enforcement of the naval blockade of Iranian ports.

“The US naval blockade has been in place for months and is professionally communicated to all international mariners,” CENTCOM said.

“Vessels that refuse to comply with blockade enforcement receive multiple warnings, with ample opportunity to comply.

“American forces remain highly vigilant, focused, and professional while fully enforcing the naval blockade against Iran.”

Iran’s complaint was submitted by Seyed Ali Mousavi, its ambassador to the IMO, and circulated to member states on Oct. 9, according to a copy reviewed by Fox News Digital.

Tehran also accused American forces of turning the maritime safety channel into an “instrument of military intimidation and psychological pressure against civilian crews.”

The letter cited commercial vessels, shipping companies and maritime operators but provided no recordings, transcripts or specific details of the alleged exchanges. Fox News Digital could not independently verify the accusations.

“Seafarers are not trained for combat, and they are not guilty of any conflicts that are happening around the world,” Dominguez said.

Morning Report delivers the latest news, videos, photos and more.

Please provide a valid email.

By clicking above you agree to the Terms of Use and Privacy Policy.

“And we have seen this in several parts of the world where Channel 16, that should not be used for this kind of communication, starts receiving messages that may be perceived as actually threatening or that are outside the remit of why it was created.”

Iran also asked the IMO to raise its allegations with member states and relevant international organizations, potentially including the International Telecommunication Union.

Dominguez said the IMO could review its regulations and procedures to determine whether stronger safeguards are needed, though he did not announce a formal investigation.

“Our role here at IMO is that when those situations take place, we will then look into any technical measures or any operational aspects that we may need to clarify further within our regulatory framework,” he said, stressing that member states have equal rights to raise concerns, regardless of the conflict.

“We have a responsibility, and I have a duty as well, to circulate letters and notes that the countries actually put forward when they’re also being affected.”

🚫 CLAIM: Iran's ambassador to the International Maritime Organization recently claimed that the U.S. military is using "threatening, abusive, and provocative language" against Iranian mariners and causing "serious stress and psychological pressure to civilian crews." This is… pic.twitter.com/dLP1Fg82I3

“We take all that information, meet at the level of different meetings of the organization and have the discussions,” Dominguez added.

“If it’s demonstrated that we probably need to improve our rules in order to avoid communications issues, or that we need to enhance the knowledge of how these channels should be used, that is a role for us.”

The IMO had recorded 100 confirmed maritime incidents across the region as of Oct. 9, with 24 seafarers killed since the conflict began Feb. 28. Dominguez also warned that fraudulent ship registrations and false flags have become major contributors to the danger.

“What we’ve also seen right now is an increase in fraudulent registries with false flags that are taking the risk and acting as shuttle tankers in order to bring goods in and out,” he said. “That’s one of the reasons that we’re seeing an escalation.

“And it’s the irresponsible shipowners that are taking the risk in order to actually be able to trade and move some of the goods and the cargoes.”

“For me, any single case, any vessel that is attacked, any life of a seafarer that is lost, is a critical situation for me, because they are all relevant, they are all important.”

Despite the confrontation, Dominguez said diplomatic channels with Iran remain open, though he has no direct contact with the Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps.

“I have communications with all the member states of IMO, and that includes the Islamic Republic of Iran,” he said.

“Of course, that’s through the diplomatic channels. I don’t have direct contact with the IRGC.

“I have conversations with them and they respond to my messages. You know, the information flows. What is difficult is to get final decisions because of the conflict that is ongoing.”

Fox News Digital has reached out to the Iranian embassy for comment.

This is… pic.twitter.com/dLP1Fg82I3

“We take all that information, meet at the level of different meetings of the organization and have the discussions,” Dominguez added.

“If it’s demonstrated that we probably need to improve our rules in order to avoid communications issues, or that we need to enhance the knowledge of how these channels should be used, that is a role for us.”

The IMO had recorded 100 confirmed maritime incidents across the region as of Oct. 9, with 24 seafarers killed since the conflict began Feb. 28. Dominguez also warned that fraudulent ship registrations and false flags have become major contributors to the danger.

“What we’ve also seen right now is an increase in fraudulent registries with false flags that are taking the risk and acting as shuttle tankers in order to bring goods in and out,” he said. “That’s one of the reasons that we’re seeing an escalation.

Despite the confrontation, Dominguez said diplomatic channels with Iran remain open, though he has no direct contact with the Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps.

“I have communications with all the member states of IMO, and that includes the Islamic Republic of Iran,” he said.

“Of course, that’s through the diplomatic channels. I don’t have direct contact with the IRGC.

“I have conversations with them and they respond to my messages. You know, the information flows. What is difficult is to get final decisions because of the conflict that is ongoing.”

Fox News Digital has reached out to the Iranian embassy for comment.

Two and a half hours, with one intermission. At the Hudson Theatre.

“Other Desert Cities,” like so many plays, is about a family with issues, to say the very least.

A free-spirited Manhattan writer named Brooke jets to sunny Palm Springs to visit her well-to-do mom, dad, TV producer brother and leftist aunt for Christmas. She’s very New York, they’re very California circa 2004.

Her buttoned-up Republican parents were close friends of Ronald and Nancy Reagan from their days working alongside them in Hollywood — mom as a screenwriter with her sister, and dad as an actor like Ronnie.

Now, their downcast daughter has brought along a surprise lump of coal as a present: galleys of her new memoir, which airs their dirtiest laundry. Those toxic pages have the potential to destroy them.

But the likeable enough Broadway revival of Jon Robin Baitz’s sharp-tongued drama, which opened Sunday night at the Hudson Theatre, takes these people’s competing personalities way too far. Quite by accident, everybody in this midcentury modern home — not just Brooke — becomes the black sheep.

Director John Benjamin Hickey’s discordant production starring Julia Louis-Dreyfus, Allison Janney, Ed Harris, Joe Keery and Lily Rabe fails to click when it’s anything more than one person tossing off mean zingers.

Each actor has their moments, most are fine and one is excellent. Not for a second, however, does anybody believe that the Wyeths are a real family or something other than an impressive assemblage of celebrities.

Making her Broadway debut, Louis-Dreyfus has the toughest assignment as Polly, one of those viperous, monster mothers that are a hallmark of the American theater. The formidable Stockard Channing played her on Broadway last time, and I saw Deanna Dunagan of “August: Osage County” don the tennis dress in Chicago 13 years ago.

Louis-Dreyfus has the requisite comic chops, obviously. She is one of the greatest funnywomen of all time. And you can understand why they’d clamor for the actress who played unhinged VP Selina Meyer to take her on.

After Brooke (Rabe) arrives to a tellingly contrasting image — a spiky Christmas tree situated in front of idyllic palms behind the window — the early goings are terrifically funny.

The “Veep” and “Seinfeld” dynamo can bat a line like “this water needs vodka for flavor” right out of the park.

But once Brooke reveals that the book she’s been working on is not a novel after all, but an explosive tell-all, the jokes subside and the topic of her dead brother Henry bubbles up. The production unfortunately cools down.

Decades earlier, when Brooke was a little girl, Henry joined an extremist group and later killed himself — a stain on the picture-frame-insert-perfect family. Brooke, who’s been cobbling together magazine travel pieces to make ends meet, has decided to finally use her writing to deal with the trauma of her past, which she believes her parents directly caused. And from there, it’s bombshell, bombshell, bombshell.

What’s odd is that in this revival, the earth-shaking revelations aren’t as energizing as the earlier one-liners. Sure, the story holds our interest, especially if you don’t know where it’s going. Baitz’s play is twisty. But don’t go in expecting to gasp.

Vital moments aren’t directed tightly or focused enough by Hickey. And his cast seems left to their own devices.

Nobody is bad. But everybody is mismatched and out of sync.

The down-on-the-ranch Harris as Polly’s husband Lyman has that unteachable Robert Redford quality you’d expect of an old-school star who’s taken refuge in the mountains. Unlike Polly, Lyman chooses passivity. And so Harris can get by on presence alone.

Janney brings a much-needed jolt to the large living room as Aunt Silda, a recovering alcoholic who hilariously cuts through Polly’s BS with exceptional wit. That is, until her own wise-cracking character has a life-altering shift and the actress recedes like most everybody else does.

One person who cannot be marked down for lack of intensity is Rabe, who’s sadly been away from Broadway hiding out in Ryan Murphy’s dungeon for 14 years. Stalking the stage like she’s at an Old West shootout, Rabe is a towering stage presence, and here she goes absolutely nuclear. Yet her enthusiasm creates an equal-but-opposite problem as Louis-Dreyfus’ hesitancy: During the climax, Rabe is in full-Medea mode while the others are quipping away on an episode of “Arrested Development.”

The strangest thing is that the revival’s stand-out is the guy from “Stranger Things.” Keery, a real talent, plays Brooke’s younger brother Trip, whom the family mocks for being a part of a lousy TV show called “Jury of Your Peers.”

Keery ably commands the stage during his riveting second act speech when Trip finally vomits out his repressed feelings about his screwed-up clan and reveals himself to be the only relative with his head on straight. That scorcher received the only extended applause of the night. Well deserved.

Baitz’s script still shines through, and is a pleasure to watch under the majority of circumstances. But Hickey’s placid revival too easily caves to its environment — dry, beautiful, relaxing and fun — when what it should be doing is fighting like hell against it.

FOXBOROUGH, Mass. — There were not many positives for the Jets to take away from Sunday’s 26-19 loss to the Patriots, but they got another standout performance from one of their rookie first-round picks.

This week, it was Omar Cooper Jr.’s turn. The wide receiver returned from a high-ankle sprain to have a huge day for the Jets. Cooper had six catches for 103 yards and a touchdown in his first game since Week 1.

Text with Brian Costello all season as he brings Sports+ subscribers the latest Jets intel from on the field and off.

“It was a great feeling,” Cooper said. “It felt good to finally be back out there.”

Cooper’s debut got cut short in the Week 1 win over the Titans. He had a 30-yard catch on the first drive of the game but sprained his ankle on the play. The injury landed him on IR and he had to watch the past four weeks.

On Sunday, he scored the only touchdown for the Jets, a 48-yard pass from Geno Smith in the third quarter. Cooper was routinely open and led the team in catches and receiving yards.

“I think Omar did a tremendous job of coming back from injury, fought just to get back out there,” Smith said. “What he did is showcase who he is. He’s a playmaker. He’s a guy who finds ways to make catches, and the tough catches, he makes them look easy. Really impressed with the way that he performed and looking forward to building on that.”

Smith is the latest Jets rookie to have a big game. The Jets drafted three players in the first round this year and each has had a big game. Edge David Bailey, the No. 2 overall pick, had three sacks in the win over the Browns last week. Tight end Kenyon Sadiq, the No. 16 pick, had 105 yards and a touchdown in the loss to the Lions. Cooper, the No. 30 pick, said he gained confidence in that Week 1 game even if it was cut short.

“I would definitely say that Titans game, coming up you have to get that confidence,” Cooper said. “I feel like that catch allowed me to get that confidence. You’re supposed to be here and just trusting in my abilities.”

Cooper and Sadiq are the third rookie tandem in Jets history to each record a 100-yard receiving game in a season. Rich Caster and Eddie Bell did it in 1970 and Garrett Wilson and Breece Hall did it in 2022.

news.originalContent:

FOXBOROUGH, Mass. — A week after the Jets sacked Cleveland’s Deshaun Watson eight times, they were unable to come up with any against New England quarterback Drake Maye in a 26-19 loss Sunday.

“It’s tough to explain, to be honest with you,’’ Jets coach Aaron Glenn said after the shutout on defense. “I have all the confidence in the world in our front and being able to cause havoc.”

Text with Brian Costello all season as he brings Sports+ subscribers the latest Jets intel from on the field and off.

It didn’t happen Sunday — and that’s even with the Patriots losing three offensive linemen to injuries during the game, as Morgan Moses, Alijah Vera-Tucker and Ben Brown all were unable to finish the game.

David Bailey, who had three sacks versus the Browns, forced a fumble in the loss but was unable to get Maye to the ground, like the rest of his teammates.

Bailey, like Glenn, credited New England’s chipping ability, especially once they were short-handed.

And Demario Davis said Maye’s skill set made it difficult to finish the job. “Maye is a very savvy quarterback,’’ he said. “We knew that going in.”

Glenn was impressed by Maye’s ability stay up even when the Jets appeared to have him in their grasp. “We’ve got to do a better job,’’ he said.

The Patriots also used a strong running game to keep the pressure off Maye, who was able to elude defenders and break away when needed.

“He does a good job getting rid of the ball,’’ Davis said. “They were able to stay in favorable situations where he didn’t have to hold the ball long. He did a good job extending plays and keeping his eyes down the field … They’re very well-coached. That’s why they were where they were last year.”

At the half, Braelon Allen had 12 carries for 65 yards and a pair of receptions for 26 more yards.

But the back was barely visible in the second half, getting just five rushes for 13 yards — and no catches — as the Jets got away from the running game.

“He was popping runs,’’ Glenn said of the early part of the game. “That’s got to continue, but down 10 [points], you have to make sure you get back in the game. We were very aware of how he was running the ball, but it was time to get the ball down the field.”

Glenn lamented the work of the special teams — outside of Jason Sanders, who made all four of his field goal attempts, the longest one 42 yards.

The Jets didn’t get much from their return game and allowed two good returns by Corey Kiner — including after a Sanders field goal cut it to 23-16 with 7:20 to go.

LB Kiko Mauigoa left with a thigh injury and didn’t return.

news.originalContent:
Claude creator says fund could used for donations to NGOs and ‘direct distributions to specific populations’.

Anthropic has pledged to commit 5 percent of its shares to a new fund dedicated to the public good, with plans to increase the contribution as the artificial intelligence giant’s market value grows.

The creator of the AI assistant Claude announced the new “Anthropic Public Benefit Fund” on Sunday as tech firms face intense scrutiny over the potential dangers posed by the frontier technology.

In a blog post, Anthropic said it was committing 5 percent of company shares with immediate effect, subject to stockholder approval, with an additional 2 percent to be added “at the board’s discretion” for every 50 percent increase in the company’s value.

“Because of the way the Fund is structured, the more Anthropic grows, the larger the share of the company that can be dedicated expressly to the public good,” the San Francisco-based firm said.

“It is common practice for tech companies to offer escalating compensation awards to their executives. We are instead directing that equity to the public benefit.”

Anthropic said the fund could be used to make donations to traditional nonprofits, as well as “direct distributions to specific populations”.

It said labour market disruption due to AI could be among the causes addressed by the fund.

“Anthropic has already committed $200 million to studying and addressing this issue, but given the pace of AI progress, bolder approaches may be needed,” the company said.

“The Fund will have the versatility to pursue them.”

Anthropic, officially registered as a “public benefit corporation” in the US state of Delaware, said the fund would not be used for lobbying or political donations, either in the United States or overseas.

Founded in 2021 by former employees of ChatGPT creator OpenAI, Anthropic is preparing for what could be the largest public initial offering in history. It is expected to list on the US stock market before the end of 2026, with analysts forecasting a valuation exceeding $2 trillion.

The company’s charter requires its leadership to balance shareholder returns with responsible AI development.

The breakneck speed of AI development has prompted widespread anxiety about possible negative downstream effects on society, including the job market.

In a report published last month, consulting firm McKinsey estimated that up to 11 million American workers may need to switch careers over the next decade due to AI-driven automation.

news.originalContent:
US president accuses Ukrainian leader of not wanting to end the war, as Zelenskyy speaks with Washington envoys.

United States President Donald Trump has defended sanction waivers for Russia, saying he wants to keep Moscow at the bargaining table and accusing his counterpart in Kyiv of not wanting to end the war in Ukraine.

Trump made the comments on Truth Social on Sunday in response to criticism of his decision to block numerous sanctions on Russia just days before they were due to take effect.

“My decision on Russia is a very simple one. I am in the process of negotiating Peace in the war between Russia and Ukraine, and don’t want to do anything that will drive, foolishly, Russia away from the bargaining table,” he said.

The move has triggered a significant diplomatic fallout between Trump and Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy over the past week.

Zelenskyy said that waiving sanctions on Russia, which launched a full-scale invasion of its neighbour in 2022, “will hurt Ukraine”, telling NBC’s Meet the Press on Sunday that it would strengthen Russian President Vladimir Putin’s war effort.

“We can’t compare me and Putin. He’s [an] aggressor. He occupied us. He killed adults and children, his soldiers. He’s a terrorist, and that’s why I hope that President Trump will be very clear with this position.”

Trump reiterated his claim that Zelenskyy does not want the war on his country to end, saying on Truth Social that Kyiv was launching attacks on diesel refineries in Russia despite knowing it was “seriously hurting the world diesel markets”.

“Zelenskyy doesn’t care, and frankly, with all of the money that Europe is famously giving him… he doesn’t want to end this war, and probably never did,” Trump wrote.

Trump announced plans on October 9 for Russia to supply more than 300,000 metric tonnes of diesel to US and global markets to tackle fuel prices that have soared since the US and Israel launched war on Iran in late February. The move led Tehran to effectively close the Strait of Hormuz, through which one-fifth of global energy exports transited before the war.

Trump’s embrace of Russian energy has angered not only Kyiv, but also European partners and many US officials, who say the move rewards Moscow while it continues its four-and-a-half-year war against Ukraine.

The Ukrainian president said on X on Sunday that he has spoken with US presidential envoys Steve Witkoff and Jared Kushner as part of “virtually non-stop communication” between the two countries’ teams aimed at the “next steps in diplomacy”.

“We are doing everything on our part to make this happen, and to ensure that America’s position is strong and helps bring peace closer. Peace that everyone, except Russia, has been waiting for over the past four and a half years,” Zelenskyy wrote.

Zelenskyy spoke with Witkoff and Kushner as Russia and Ukraine continued to strike each other’s energy sites, with Moscow leaving thousands without power, and Kyiv carrying out the largest drone attack on Russia, in St Petersburg, since the war began.

news.originalContent:
The air strike, one of Ukraine’s largest in the war, comes amid rising tensions between Kyiv and Washington.

At least one person has been killed, and five others injured after Ukraine launched more than 1,000 drones at Russia, one of Kyiv’s largest aerial strikes in the war.

St Petersburg Governor Alexander Beglov said firefighters were battling fires sparked by Sunday’s attacks on the St Petersburg oil terminal, the Ruchi oil depot and industrial warehouses in the Kolpinsky district south of the city.

The governor said the “massive” strike killed at least one person and injured five, and that several residential buildings and two houses were also hit.

The attack disrupted flights at St Petersburg’s main airport, one of the country’s busiest, which was restricting operations “for safety reasons”, Beglov said.

Russian e-commerce company Ozon said there was a fire at its logistics hub in St Petersburg. The internet company VK said drones attacked its data centre in the broader Leningrad region, adding that normal services were available to users.

Leningrad Governor Alexander Drozdenko said 145 drones had been shot down and about 20,000 people were without electricity following the drone raid.

The Ministry of Defence said 1,015 Ukrainian drones were neutralised overnight over 15 Russian regions, the annexed Ukrainian peninsula of Crimea and the Black Sea.

The strikes came as tensions between Kyiv and Washington deepened, with US President Donald Trump criticising Ukraine’s attacks on Russian oil infrastructure, and the prospect of further US sanctions against Moscow still uncertain.

On Sunday, Trump defended his Friday decision to put a hold on implementing new sanctions on Russia, saying he did not want to do anything that would “foolishly” drive Moscow “away from the bargaining table”.

In a social media post, the US president said he believed new sanctions would undermine negotiations to bring about a diplomatic end to Moscow’s war on Ukraine, refuting bipartisan criticism that he was favouring Russian President Vladimir Putin’s interests over Kyiv’s.

Trump also lashed out at Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy, who has been critical of Trump’s recent outreach to Putin, for launching strikes on Russian energy infrastructure, claiming Zelenskyy “doesn’t want to end this war”.

Trump had announced on October 11 that Russia and Ukraine agreed to an “energy ceasefire”, but offered no details. Zelenskyy told The Financial Times that he was “done” with the ceasefire a few days later, after holding off on striking Russia’s energy facilities while Moscow had continued attacking Ukraine’s.

Zelenskyy wrote on X on Sunday that Russia had attacked Ukraine’s energy, oil and gas sectors 76 times in the week since Trump’s announcement.

Energy facilities in four Ukrainian regions were struck overnight, leaving tens of thousands of families without power, he said, accusing Russia of trying to “cause a blackout”.

“America should see that Russia is not taking any reciprocal steps in response to sanctions relief or agreements,” he said.

Speaking on NBC’s Meet the Press on Sunday, Zelenskyy said that waiving sanctions against Russia would strengthen Putin’s war effort. He also said US-Ukraine intelligence sharing had resumed after being “blocked for some period of time”.

Zelenskyy said that while he trusted Trump, siding with Moscow would be a tragedy and a “historic mistake” for Washington.

Later on Sunday, Zelenskyy said on social media that he had spoken with US presidential envoys Steve Witkoff and Jared Kushner about the results of an October 9 meeting between Washington and Kyiv’s negotiating teams in Miami, as well as the “next steps in diplomacy”.

Meanwhile, a Russian air strike ⁠killed ⁠a woman in the Ukrainian capital, Kyiv, overnight while also hitting a subway station and damaging a 25-storey residential ⁠building, Mayor Vitali Klitschko said on Telegram on Monday.

The attack, which also hit non-residential buildings and a medical facility, ‌injured three other people in Kyiv, Klitschko said.

Two Russian attacks on the southern Ukrainian city of Zaporizhzhia killed a woman and wounded at least two other people, including a six-year-old girl, local officials said on Sunday.

In another post on X on Sunday, Zelenskyy said Russian strikes on residential buildings had killed two people and injured 12, including two children, in Volyn.

“This morning, there was a strike on an agricultural enterprise in Volyn. All necessary services are working at the site,” he said.

“In total, over this past week, the Russians have attacked Ukraine with almost 2,700 attack drones, 1,700 aerial bombs, and 66 missiles, most of them ballistic,” the Ukrainian president wrote.

news.originalContent:
Kenyan health authorities say latest patient was likely exposed to the country’s first Ebola case.

Kenyan health authorities say an eighth Ebola case has been detected in the East African nation.

Director-General for Health Patrick Amoth told Kenya’s Citizen TV that of the 38 people tested on Sunday, one had returned a positive result.

“He is a 49-year-old man who is not a healthcare worker. He developed fever, headache and muscle pain,” he said.

Amoth said the man, who worked as a patient attendant cleaning utensils and linens, was likely exposed to Kenya’s first Ebola case, discovered earlier this month.

He developed symptoms on Saturday, was quarantined and tested for the virus, a Ministry of Health source said.

The ministry reported four new cases on Saturday, three of whom were health workers who treated the country’s first Ebola patient, a man who travelled from the Democratic Republic of the Congo (DRC) to Nairobi and died at a Nairobi hospital on October 5.

In a post on X, the ministry said the fourth person was related to the deceased patient.

Kenya has been on heightened alert, as the Ebola outbreak has spilled across the border from the DRC. The current outbreak is of the Bundibugyo strain of the virus, for which there is no vaccine or specific treatment.

The DRC has recorded at least 9,400 cases, including more than 4,500 deaths, in the deadliest outbreak in the country’s history, which started in May.

Ituri province in eastern DRC remains the disease’s epicentre, accounting for almost three quarters of confirmed cases, according to the government’s most recent data. It announced on Sunday that the virus has reached an eighth province, North Ubangi.

State-run news agency ACP reported on Sunday that authorities in North Kivu province, where the World Health Organization said substantial transmission continues, are introducing a one-week ban from Monday on people entering the province from Ituri in an effort to slow the spread.

Other measures set to be introduced include restrictions on passenger numbers in cars and on motorbikes and suspension of large public gatherings.

Neighbouring Uganda recorded 20 confirmed cases, including 15 imported from the DRC, and two deaths, before it was declared Ebola-free in August.

news.originalSummary: در پی غرق شدن یک کشتی کانتینربر در تنگه هرمز و ریختن محتویاتش در دریا، پلیس فضای مجازی (فتا) درباره احتمال کلاهبرداری فروش «آیفون دریایی» هشدار داده است. این هشدار پس از انتشار تصاویری از گروهی منتشر شد که پس از غرق شدن یک کشتی کانتینربر با پرچم سنگاپور محتویاتش را از آب جمع‌آوری می‌کردند. گزارش‌هایی هم درباره وجود «کالای لوکس، از جمله آیفون ۱۸» در میان محموله این کشتی منتشر شده بود.

news.title: خودروهای سوخته و شیشه‌های خردشده در خیابان‌های پاریس؛ ۱۸۰۰ نفر بازداشت شدند
news.originalSummary:
فرانسه روز یکشنبه، پس از یک روز ناآرامی و تظاهرات، با صحنه‌هایی از ویرانی گسترده از خواب برخاست؛ ویترین‌های خردشده، خودروهای سوخته، دوچرخه‌های زغال‌شده و توده‌هایی از خرده‌شیشه و آوار در پیاده‌روهای پاریس به چشم می‌خورد.

روز شنبه، در حالی که حدود ۵۵۰ هزار معترض در تظاهراتی که عمدتاً مسالمت‌آمیز بود به خیابان‌ها آمده بودند، پلیس نزدیک به ۱۸۰۰ نفر را بازداشت کرد.

معترضان به افزایش قیمت سوخت، هزینه‌های زندگی و تضعیف خدمات عمومی، از جمله وضعیت مدارس، اعتراض داشتند.

همچنین گروه‌هایی از آشوبگران که برخی از آن‌ها لباس سیاه پوشیده و صورت خود را با ماسک یا پوشش‌های مخصوص پوشانده بودند، در پاریس، مارسی و دیگر شهرها و شهرک‌ها ظاهر شدند و برخی از آن‌ها اقدام به آتش زدن خودروها و ساختمان‌ها کردند.

غارت گسترده‌ای در شهرهای پاریس، مارسی و لیل، و همچنین مناطق دیگر رخ داد.

در پاریس، معترضان با پلیس ضدشورش درگیر شدند؛ پلیس نیز برای متفرق کردن جمعیت از گاز اشک‌آور و ماشین‌های آب‌پاش استفاده کرد. در طول روز، برخی گروه‌ها در خیابان‌ها آتش روشن کردند و خودروها را به آتش کشیدند. دست‌کم یک رستوران در آتش سوخت و کاملاً ویران شد؛ همچنین خبرنگاران بی‌بی‌سی شاهد درگیری‌هایی میان برخی از گروه‌ها بودند.

پلیس ضدشورش در مرکز پاریس به سمت جمعیتی هجوم برد و چندین نفر را با باتون مورد ضرب‌وشتم قرار داد.

محمد اوزدن، از ساکنان پاریس، به خبرگزاری فرانسه گفت: «انگار جنگ شده است.»

یکی دیگر از ساکنان به نام آنیتا گراسیت گفت دیدن گروه‌هایی از جوانان که «همه چیز را در هم می‌شکنند و هیچ ترسی هم از مجازات ندارند»، «وحشتناک» بود.

ماریس، زنی که در آن نزدیکی زندگی می‌کند و تنها به ذکر نام کوچک خود بسنده کرد، به بی‌بی‌سی گفت که غارتگران «با افتخار سبدهای خرید فروشگاه‌ها را که پر از کالا بود با خود می‌بردند و به دزدی‌هایشان می‌خندیدند.»

گزیده‌ای از مهم‌ترین خبرها، گزارش‌های میدانی و گفت‌وگوهای اختصاصی را هر هفته در ایمیل خود دریافت کنید.

در جنوب فرانسه، در شهر مارسی، معترضان با استفاده از یک حصار فلزی به عنوان وسیله‌ای برای کوبیدن درها، وارد ساختمان شهرداری شدند. به گفته پلیس، در شهر لیل نیز یک شعبه رستوران مک‌دونالد به آتش کشیده شد و به یک فروشگاه محصولات اپل نیز دستبرد زده و غارت شد.

در شبکه‌‌های اجتماعی تصاویری از آتش‌سوزی ساختمان‌های دولتی منتشر شده است.

دولت فرانسه این تحولات را «تشدید خشونت‌ها» توصیف کرد.

در شهر لیموژ، ساختمان شهرداری در آتش سوخت و فروریخت.

موریس بارات، فرماندار بخش اوت-وین، گفت که «گروهی اوباش» به‌طور «عمدی» این بنای ۱۴۳ ساله را به آتش کشیده‌اند.

وزارت کشور فرانسه اعلام کرد که بیش از ۵۰۰ افسر پلیس، ژاندارم و آتش‌نشان در ناآرامی‌های روز شنبه زخمی شدند.

فدراسیون خرده‌فروشی و تجارت اعلام کرد که حدود ۱۵۰۰ مغازه و خرده‌فروش نیز در این ناآرامی‌ها آسیب دیده‌اند.

صبح یکشنبه در پاریس، ساکنان از عواقب این ناآرامی‌ها، از جمله شیشه‌های خرد شده فروشگاه‌های طراحان از جمله رالف لورن، گوچی و ورساچه، بازدید کردند.

مغازه‌داران صبح زود با جارو بیرون آمده بودند و همزمان با شروع پاکسازی، خرده شیشه‌های بزرگ را جمع می‌کردند. کامیون‌های حمل زباله در برخی از خیابان‌های بزرگتر برای پاکسازی برخی از آوارها به راه خود ادامه دادند.

بسیاری از مغازه‌ها با گرافیتی‌هایی پوشیده شده بودند که برخی از آنها نوشته بودند «از ثروتمندان مالیات بگیرید» و «ثروتمندان را بخورید».

منبع تصویر، Hesham Elsherif/Anadolu via Getty Images

بی‌بی‌سی از یک فروشگاه لباس در نزدیکی میدان ریپوبلیک (جمهوری) بازدید کرد که مورد غارت قرار گرفته بود و انبوهی از لباس و مبلمان در سراسر مغازه پراکنده شده بود.

صاحب پریشان مغازه به بی‌بی‌سی گفت که در دوربین مداربسته، غارتگرانی را دیده است که کمی بیش از یک ساعت و نیم در مغازه بوده‌اند و در این مدت هیچ پلیسی را در این جریان ندیده است.

این صاحب مغازه که نخواست نامش فاش شود به بی‌بی‌سی گفت که باور ندارد هیچ یک از کسانی که مغازه را سرقت کردند، معترضان واقعی علیه شرایط مدرسه یا هزینه‌های زندگی باشند. او گفت که غارتگران از تظاهرات سوءاستفاده می‌کردند.

در پاریس، راهپیمایی اصلی در ساعات بعدازظهر عمدتا مسالمت‌آمیز به نظر می‌رسید. گروهی از جوانان به بی‌بی‌سی گفتند که «صلح‌طلب» هستند و «فقط می‌خواهند اوضاع را تغییر دهند اما هیچ‌چیز تغییر نمی‌کند.»

با این حال، با گذشت زمان، گروه‌هایی در خیابان‌ها آتش روشن کردند و خودروها را به آتش کشیدند. این حوادث در مکان‌های شناخته‌شده مرکز شهر از جمله میدان جمهوری رخ داد.

در مرکز پاریس، پلیس ضدشورش به جمعیت یورش برد و با باتوم معترضان را زد.

در شهر لیون، گرگوری دوسه، شهردار، آتش‌زدن دفتر گردشگری شهر را «فاجعه» خواند. او به شبکه بی‌اف‌ام‌تی‌وی گفت: «این اتفاق قلب ما را به درد می‌آورد چون این ساختمان تاریخی بسیار شناخته‌شده و نمادین است.»

پلیس این شهر می‌گوید که «افراد مهاجم» مانع شدند آتش‌نشانان بتوانند در امنیت آتش را مهار کنند.

رژی ژوانیکو، شهردار سن‌اتین در جنوب شرقی فرانسه، در شبکه‌های اجتماعی نوشت که دست یک جوان بر اثر انفجار یک ماده منفجره کوچک قطع شده است. او گفت که «چنین فاجعه‌ای هرگز نباید اتفاق می‌افتاد.»

در هفته‌های اخیر، صدها هزار دانش‌آموز در اعتراض به کمبود معلم و فرسودگی امکانات دبیرستان‌های فرانسه به خیابان‌ها آمده‌اند. این مدارس محل تحصیل نوجوانان ۱۵ تا ۱۸ ساله هستند.

اعضای اتحادیه‌های کارگری و گروه‌های دیگر هم اکنون به اعتراضات پیوسته‌اند.

«جلیقه‌زردها» هم که با اعتراضات سال ۲۰۱۸ به افزایش هزینه‌های زندگی شناخته می‌شوند، به اعتراضات پیوسته‌اند.

به گفته وزارت کشور فرانسه، در اعتراض‌های روز شنبه، در برخی مناطق، از جمله بخش‌هایی از پاریس و همچنین مارسی، رن، تولوز و آنژه، «افراد نقابدار» دست به «اقدامات خشونت‌آمیز هدفمند» زدند.

امانوئل مکرون، رئیس‌جمهور فرانسه، سال آینده از قدرت کناره‌گیری خواهد کرد. نظرسنجی‌ها نشان می‌دهند که انتخابات ریاست‌جمهوری ماه آوریل ممکن است به رقابت میان مارین لوپن، رهبر حزب راست افراطی اجتماع ملی، و ژان‌لوک ملانشون، رهبر حزب چپ رادیکال فرانسه تسلیم‌ناپذیر، تبدیل شود.

آقای ملانشون در تظاهرات شرکت و پلیس را متهم کرده است که به معترضان «یورش» برده است. او در عین حال غارت فروشگاه‌ها و آتش‌افروزی را محکوم کرد.

در هفته‌های اخیر، صدها هزار دانش‌آموز در اعتراض به کمبود معلم و فرسودگی امکانات دبیرستان‌های فرانسه به خیابان‌ها آمده‌اند. این مدارس محل تحصیل نوجوانان ۱۵ تا ۱۸ ساله هستند.

اعضای اتحادیه‌های کارگری و گروه‌های دیگر هم اکنون به اعتراضات پیوسته‌اند.

«جلیقه‌زردها» هم که با اعتراضات سال ۲۰۱۸ به افزایش هزینه‌های زندگی شناخته می‌شوند، به اعتراضات پیوسته‌اند.

به گفته وزارت کشور فرانسه، در اعتراض‌های روز شنبه، در برخی مناطق، از جمله بخش‌هایی از پاریس و همچنین مارسی، رن، تولوز و آنژه، «افراد نقابدار» دست به «اقدامات خشونت‌آمیز هدفمند» زدند.

امانوئل مکرون، رئیس‌جمهور فرانسه، سال آینده از قدرت کناره‌گیری خواهد کرد. نظرسنجی‌ها نشان می‌دهند که انتخابات ریاست‌جمهوری ماه آوریل ممکن است به رقابت میان مارین لوپن، رهبر حزب راست افراطی اجتماع ملی، و ژان‌لوک ملانشون، رهبر حزب چپ رادیکال فرانسه تسلیم‌ناپذیر، تبدیل شود.

آقای ملانشون در تظاهرات شرکت و پلیس را متهم کرده است که به معترضان «یورش» برده است. او در عین حال غارت فروشگاه‌ها و آتش‌افروزی را محکوم کرد.

Kansas City Chiefs cornerback Christian Roland-Wallace might think twice about his actions after he was caught throwing a punch in the fourth quarter of Sunday’s 22-6 victory against the Chargers.

Wallace was ejected during the fourth quarter after the CBS broadcast replay caught him throwing a punch at Chargers offensive tackle Alex Harkey’s helmet when he was attempting to get up after a play.

ONE OF THE STUPIDEST PLAYS YOU WILL EVER SEE:#Chiefs CB Christian Roland-Wallace was ejected after this incident against the #Chargers.He cost his team 15 yards and got himself thrown out of a crucial divisional matchup.Unbelievably dumb decision 😳 pic.twitter.com/374VIdvW8O

In the replay, Wallace was also visibly seen getting pushed by safety Jayden Hicks while delivering his left hook.

Prior to the punch, Harkey was seen pushing Wallace into Kansas City linebacker Nick Bolton at the end of the play after the whistle was blown.

Aside from being removed from the game, Wallace also received a 15-yard penalty for his action and can potentially face a suspension and fine for the punch.

Wallace finished the game four tackles, three of them logged as solo.

In what’s been a frustrating season for Los Angeles, Sunday only added to it as Los Angeles is now 0-6 to start the year.

The Chargers compiled a total of 259 yards of offense and failed to score a touchdown despite quarterback Justin Herbert putting the team one yard away from the endzone after he threw a 57-yard pass to Quentin Johnston in the third quarter.

A holding penalty on the next play moved Los Angeles back 10 yards, resulting in the team failing to break through and settling for a 30-yard field goal by Cameron Dicker.

Herbert completed 22 of 37 passes for 204 yards and threw his eighth interception of the season in the second quarter.

The running game continued to struggle as Los Angeles had only 73 yards on the ground, and Herbert was team’s leading rusher, having 26 yards on the ground.

Los Angeles also took a hit from the injury bug as wide receiver Ladd McConkey left the game early in the second quarter with a concussion after hauling in a 17-yard reception.

See more of our coverage in your search results.

Just call her mother angel.

Barbara Palvin hit the Victoria’s Secret Fashion Show 2026 runway Sunday night, strutting her stuff in a sheer pale pink dress with a matching bra and panties.

The new mom wore her hair down in waves and accessorized with oversized gold hoops, adorned with the iconic lingerie label’s logo.

The star, 33, has been a long time VS model, but her turn on the catwalk this year is especially notable as she welcomed her first child just six weeks ago. Palvin gave birth to a baby girl named Sylvie on Sept. 7, writing on Instagram, “We took Labor Day literally this year” with husband Dylan Sprouse.

Ahead of the show, Page Six Style chatted with Palvin backstage, where she told us, “I tell everyone: This is normal. Maternity leave is six to eight weeks; I’m six weeks tomorrow, so I’m just doing what everyone [else] is doing. And I only need to walk down a runway!”

She added, “I’m happy. I’m excited. I hope I don’t fall!”

She joins the ranks of model moms including Jasmine Tookes, who walked the runway last year while nine months pregnant and Heidi Klum, who shocked fans when she revealed that she was secretly pregnant with daughter Leni when she wore the Fantasy Bra in 2003.

Klum also returned to the runway eight weeks after giving birth to son Henry in 2005 and five weeks after giving birth to Lou Samuel in 2009. Adriana Lima was similarly dedicated, making her first runway walk as a mom eight weeks after giving birth to daughter Valentina in 2008 and two months after her second child in 2012.

Palvin and Sprouse announced in May that they were starting a family, with the model debuting her bump on the Cannes Film Festival red carpet in a gorgeous light blue Miu Miu gown trimmed in feathers.

Victoria’s Secret announced that Palvin would once again appear in her skivvies just days before the show with a cheeky Instagram video of the star pushing a stroller with the caption, “Motherhood looks good on you, @realbarbarapalvin. So does the runway—see you in LA.”

Sprouse supported his spouse, writing on Instagram, “Proud of my missus, jumping right into the vs fashion show post-birth. Built different. I don’t know where you find the energy but damn!”

The former Disney Channel star is known for his over-the-top support of his now-wife, previously bringing cut-outs of their pets to the pink carpet and delivered her hamburgers directly at the show.

My wonderful husband will be here tonight,” Palvin confirmed to us ahead of the show. “I don’t know what he’s planning — hopefully nothing, because he has to be taking care of our baby girl right now!”

Palvin made her runway debut for Prada when she was just 17 years old and, two years later, made her Victoria’s Secret debut. While she didn’t return to the VS runway until 2018, she was then officially crowned an Angel the following year and walked in the 2024 and 2025 shows.

news.originalContent:

Any chance of Ben Simmons making a comeback this season will have to wait until next season.

The Sacramento Kings announced on Sunday that an MRI confirmed Simmons has suffered a torn right Achilles injury during practice.

“Sacramento Kings guard Ben Simmons was injured during a live drill in practice on Sunday, Oct. 18. An MRI revealed a torn right Achilles tendon. Simmons will undergo surgery,” the Kings announced in a press release this afternoon.

Simmons signed a one-year $3.5 million deal with the Kings last month after spending last year as an unsigned free agent. The deal was reportedly a non-guaranteed contract that would’ve paid him $1 million if he made the opening night roster.

Simmons was once a No.1 overall pick in the NBA Draft in 2016 but spent his career hampered by injuries, including a right foot fracture in 2016-2017, as well as constant knee and leg injuries from 2021-2025.

This season, he was expected to be a backup point guard, behind rookie Darius Acuff Jr., who’s played in four of the Kings’ preseason games.

Simmons has appeared in two preseason games this season and recently had 25 minutes of playing time last Friday when he scored 14 points, with eight rebounds, seven assists, and one steal against the San Antonio Spurs.

The Kings are set to open their season this Wednesday when they travel to Los Angeles to play the Clippers.
